source: FICTIONAL desktop-PC maintenance simulation. Illustrative only - not real maintenance advice. Hardware facts to be validated against an equipment source before the main study.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU rocker switch at the rear of the case to O (off).
steps.explanation: The switch isolates mains power from the motherboard. A spinning fan must never be unplugged while the board is powered.

steps.instruction: Remove the thumbscrew at the bottom-right corner of the side panel.
steps.explanation: The thumbscrew is the only fastener holding the panel. Loosening it by hand avoids tools scratching the paint.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel off to open the case.
steps.explanation: The panel rides on slots along the case edge. Sliding it back first, then lifting, avoids bending the sheet metal.

steps.instruction: Touch the bare metal of the case to discharge static.
steps.explanation: Static from your body can damage the fan's motor driver even though no spark is visible. Bare case metal equalises the charge.

steps.instruction: Unplug the front fan's power cable from the header on the fan corner.
steps.explanation: The header feeds the fan's tachometer and speed control. Pulling the connector body, not the wires, keeps the pins straight.

steps.instruction: Remove the four screws at the corners of the fan mount.
steps.explanation: Four screws hold the fan against the front mount. Removing them in the marked order keeps the fan square in its frame.

steps.instruction: Lift the old fan out of the front mount.
steps.explanation: The fan is now held by nothing but its frame. Lifting it straight out avoids scraping the dust shroud.

steps.instruction: Fit the new fan into the front mount.
steps.explanation: The fan's arrow marking shows airflow direction, front to back, so the case breathes the way the ducts were designed.

steps.instruction: Refit the four screws at the corners of the fan mount.
steps.explanation: Tightening all four evenly stops the fan frame rattling against the mount when it spins up.

steps.instruction: Plug the fan's power cable back into the header.
steps.explanation: The header is keyed so the plug only fits one way. A seated plug lets the motherboard read the fan's speed.

steps.instruction: Slide the side panel back on until it clicks home.
steps.explanation: Closing the case before power is restored keeps dust out and the airflow path intact.

steps.instruction: Flip the PSU power switch back to I (on).
steps.explanation: Power is restored only after every part is secured, so the new fan spins up in a fully assembled machine.

hazard.message: STATIC WARNING: charge detected on your wrist. Discharge on the case metal before touching the fan!
